A **linear program** (LP) optimizes a linear objective subject to linear constraints. It
is the workhorse of Operations Research: integer-programming solvers and decomposition
methods solve LPs over and over, and many planning problems are LPs themselves.

All pages in this category use the same small example, a workshop making chairs and
tables, so the numbers carry over from page to page:
$$
\max\ 3x_1 + 4x_2 \quad\text{s.t.}\quad x_1 + 2x_2 \le 8 \ (\text{wood}),\quad
2x_1 + x_2 \le 7 \ (\text{labor}),\quad x_1, x_2 \ge 0 .
$$
Its optimum is $x^\star = (2, 3)$ with profit $18$.

Prerequisite: the [Foundations](../foundations/index.qmd) pages, especially
[Polyhedra and Their Vertices](../foundations/polyhedra/polyhedra-and-vertices.qmd) and
[Farkas' Lemma](../foundations/polyhedra/farkas-lemma.qmd).
